extracted.intended_audience: state air pollution control agencies, state plan developers, and affected EGU owners/operators
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for developing and submitting state plans under CAA section 111(d) for existing electric generating units (EGUs), including how to set presumptively approvable standards of performance, compliance dates, extensions, and use of remaining-useful-life and other factors. Covers subcategory-specific BSER determinations, required plan elements, monitoring/reporting, and procedural requirements for extension and RULOF demonstrations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance period and demonstration timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Affected EGUs demonstrate compliance on an annual (calendar-year) basis; the compliance period is one calendar year. For a compliance period (calendar year) the compliance demonstration must occur by March 1 of the following year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: For units with a compliance date of Jan 1, 2030, the first compliance period is Jan 1–Dec 31, 2030 and the compliance demonstration is due by March 1, 2031. Units must start monitoring and reporting as of the compliance date even though the demonstration is made at the end of the calendar year.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standards of performance unit format (rate or mass) and translation requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards of performance must be established as either a rate or, for affected EGUs in certain subcategories, a mass of emissions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a state allows mass-based compliance, it must first calculate the rate-based emission limitation that corresponds to the presumptive standard of performance and then explain how it translated that rate-based limitation into the mass that constitutes the EGU's standard. See section X.D for more on demonstrating compliance where states incorporate compliance flexibilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Long-term coal-fired steam generating units BSER (CCS 90% capture) and degree of emission limitation
rubrics_metrics.description: For long-term coal-fired steam generating units (those not meeting medium-term specs) the Best System of Emission Reduction (BSER) is CCS with 90 percent capture, which corresponds to an 88.4 percent reduction in CO2 emission rate on a lb CO2/MWh-gross basis (annual calendar-year basis).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establishing a standard: (1) establish source-specific baseline emission performance; (2) apply the degree of emission limitation (complement 11.6%) to baseline. Example: baseline 2,000 lb CO2/MWh -> presumptively approvable standard = 2,000 * 0.116 = 232 lb CO2/MWh. EPA finalizes federally enforceable increments of progress for these units (see X.C.3).

rubrics_metrics.name: Long-term coal: federally enforceable increments of progress
rubrics_metrics.description: Affected coal-fired EGUs in the long-term subcategory must comply with federally enforceable increments of progress.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Increments of progress are described in section X.C.3 of the preamble and are required as enforceable steps toward installation/implementation of the BSER (CCS). Compliance date extension demonstrations must show increments met up to the point of delay.

rubrics_metrics.name: Medium-term coal-fired steam generating units BSER (40% natural gas co-firing) and degree of emission limitation
rubrics_metrics.description: For medium-term coal-fired units that plan to permanently cease operations before Jan 1, 2039, BSER is 40 percent natural gas co-firing on a heat-input basis, which translates to a 16 percent reduction in lb CO2/MWh-gross relative to baseline (annual calendar-year basis).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establishing a standard: (1) determine source-specific baseline emission performance; (2) multiply baseline by complement (84%) to get presumptively approvable standard. Example: baseline 2,000 lb CO2/MWh -> 2,000 * 0.84 = 1,680 lb CO2/MWh.

rubrics_metrics.name: Medium-term coal: adjustment for preexisting co-firing in baseline
rubrics_metrics.description: If baseline already reflects some natural gas co-firing, the degree of emission limitation is adjusted to achieve the additional co-firing beyond the baseline level.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: if baseline co-firing = 10% heat input, the degree of limitation is adjusted to achieve an additional 30% co-firing (i.e., reach 40%), resulting in a 12% reduction in lb CO2/MWh relative to baseline. EPA prefers adjusting the degree of limitation rather than changing the baseline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Medium-term coal: enforceable commitment to permanently cease operations
rubrics_metrics.description: If a state places an affected EGU in the medium-term coal subcategory, the state plan must include that EGU's commitment to permanently cease operating prior to Jan 1, 2039 as an enforceable requirement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The state plan must include provisions for implementation and enforcement of the commitment, including requirements for monitoring, reporting, and recordkeeping. Affected EGUs relying on cessation commitments must comply with milestones and reporting requirements described in section X.C.4, and federally enforceable increments of progress (X.C.3).

rubrics_metrics.name: Natural gas- and oil-fired steam generating units presumptive standards by load category
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA finalizes presumptive standards of performance (annual calendar-year lb CO2/MWh-gross) for intermediate and base load natural gas- and oil-fired steam generating units: intermediate load = 1,600 lb CO2/MWh-gross; base load = 1,400 lb CO2/MWh-gross.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Definitions of load subcategories are in VII.D.1. EPA chose these fixed presumptive standards because emissions data at intermediate and base load show low variability (95% of units below these thresholds). EPA finalizes the same standards for oil-fired units as for natural gas-fired units given operational similarities and fuel switching behavior.

rubrics_metrics.name: Low-load natural gas and oil BSER (uniform fuels) and degrees of emission limitation
rubrics_metrics.description: For low-load natural gas and oil-fired steam generating units EPA finalizes uniform fuels as the BSER, with degrees of emission limitation defined by fuel-specific values.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Finalized degrees: low-load natural gas-fired units = 130 lb CO2/MMBtu; low-load oil-fired units = 170 lb CO2/MMBtu. Presumptively approvable standards are consistent with these values.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance dates (final/initial compliance dates and monitoring start)
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA finalizes compliance dates for subcategories: Jan 1, 2030 for medium-term coal and natural gas/oil units; Jan 1, 2032 for long-term coal units (installing CCS). Compliance dates are the dates when affected EGUs must start monitoring and reporting for future compliance demonstrations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although monitoring/reporting starts on the compliance date, actual compliance demonstrations occur after the calendar-year compliance period ends. EPA uses 'compliance date', 'final compliance date', 'initial compliance date' interchangeably to denote when monitoring/reporting commences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance date extension mechanism: eligibility and scope
rubrics_metrics.description: States may include a mechanism in their plans to extend the compliance date for certain affected EGUs, but only where an affected EGU encounters a delay in installation of control technology that makes it impossible to commence compliance by the prescribed date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The mechanism is limited to delays entirely beyond the owner/operator's control (e.g., permitting delays, supply chain, delivery or construction delays). It is intended to address implementation delays for installing add-on controls — not to provide extra time to assess compliance strategy or subcategory assignment. States are not required to include the mechanism; absent it, a plan revision is needed to extend approved schedules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance date extension: documentation and procedural requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: To receive an extension the owner/operator must demonstrate and document (1) that relevant increments of progress were met up to the point of delay, (2) documentation that the delay is due to a third party or circumstances beyond their control (e.g., invoices, correspondence), and (3) plans to address and remedy the delay, including updated increment dates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All documentation must be submitted to the state air pollution control agency no later than 6 months prior to the compliance date. The owner/operator must notify the relevant EPA Regional Administrator at time of submission and must post the application to the Carbon Pollution Standards for EGUs website. The state agency must notify the EPA Regional Administrator of determinations; if approved, the owner/operator must post the state's determination and update website info within 30 days.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance date extension: limits, approval, and timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Extended compliance dates must be as expeditious as practicable and the maximum allowed extension under the mechanism is 1 year beyond the compliance date specified in the state plan.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the anticipated delay exceeds 1 year states can use the mechanism for up to 1 year but should initiate a state plan revision (considering RULOF) to provide an updated compliance date, subject to EPA approval. The state air pollution control agency approves or disapproves extension requests based on written determination that the owner/operator satisfied demonstration/documentation requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: RULOF — when states may apply less stringent standards or longer schedules
rubrics_metrics.description: Under CAA section 111(d) and implementing regs at 40 CFR 60.24a, states may consider remaining useful life and other factors (RULOF) to apply a less stringent standard of performance or longer compliance schedule to a particular facility, but only when fundamental differences between the facility's circumstances and the information EPA considered make it unreasonable for the facility to achieve the EPA-determined degree of emission limitation or compliance schedule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The 'fundamentally different' standard is a limited variance consistent with statutory purpose. The relevant question is whether the facility can reasonably achieve the degree of emission limitation (not merely whether it can implement the BSER).

rubrics_metrics.name: RULOF — required evaluation factors and analyses
rubrics_metrics.description: When applying RULOF to determine a less stringent standard or longer schedule, the state must evaluate systems of emission reduction using the same factors and metrics EPA considered: technical feasibility, amount of emission reductions, cost of achieving reductions, non-air quality health and environmental impacts, and energy requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: States may also consider other facility-specific factors that justified invoking RULOF and additional systems of emission reduction as appropriate. Any less stringent standard or longer schedule must be no less stringent/longer than necessary to address the fundamental difference.

rubrics_metrics.name: RULOF — enforceable operating-condition based variances and plan content
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a less stringent standard is based on an operating condition within the facility's control, the state plan must include that operating condition as an enforceable requirement and include monitoring, reporting, and recordkeeping for implementation and enforcement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example contexts include variances based on remaining useful life or utilization. The plan must make such conditions enforceable and operationally verifiable.

rubrics_metrics.name: RULOF — procedural burdens on states and stakeholder engagement
rubrics_metrics.description: States bear the burden of making and documenting demonstrations in support of less-stringent standards or longer schedules under RULOF; EPA must be able to ascertain from the state plan that the standard meets statutory and regulatory requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: States must include documentation that they conducted meaningful engagement with pertinent stakeholders (industry, small businesses, communities most affected/vulnerable). Consideration of health and environmental impacts on impacted communities is inherent in the factors (non-air quality impacts and amount of emission reduction) and should be part of meaningful engagement and reasoned decision making included in the plan.

rubrics_metrics.name: States may adopt standards more stringent or faster than EPA emission guideline
rubrics_metrics.description: States retain the ability to adopt and enforce standards of performance that are more stringent than the EPA-determined degree of emission limitation and compliance schedules that require final compliance sooner than specified in the emission guideline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: States do not need to use RULOF to apply more stringent standards or faster schedules.

rubrics_metrics.name: EPA-presumptively approvable standard floor
rubrics_metrics.description: In general, standards of performance that states establish must be no less stringent than the presumptively approvable standards specified in these emission guidelines, unless a proper RULOF demonstration justifies a limited variance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 40 CFR 60.24a(c) requires states' standards to reflect the degree of emission limitation achievable through BSER as identified by EPA; any deviation via RULOF must be justified, documented, and limited to addressing fundamental differences.
